overall: The AG found the committee properly met in executive session under Purpose 3 and did not have to release the vote tally, but violated the law with insufficiently detailed executive session minutes and ordered amendments.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to release the individual tally of member votes taken in a February 26 executive session on a policy issue.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Committee was not required to “release the individual tally of votes” taken during its February 26 executive session while the purpose for that executive session was ongoing.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee met in executive session on February 26 and March 1 without a lawful purpose, as the PEACE flag matter was not threatened litigation.
Not raised in the complaint: AG found the February 26 and March 1 executive session minutes too thin to show the substance of the discussions.
allegations.key_passage: Based on our communications with Counsel for the Committee, we understand that the minutes fail to capture much of the discussion that took place during the two executive sessions.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: AG noted that a March 1 executive session discussion of a busing company contract fit no executive session purpose.
allegations.key_passage: This discussion did not fit within any of the ten executive session purposes provided for in the Open Meeting Law and was therefore inappropriate for executive session.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Amend the February 26 and March 1 executive session minutes to the best of its ability and certify to the AG within 30 days that it has done so.
remedy_passage: Furthermore, we order the Committee to amend the minutes for its February 26 and March 1 executive sessions and to certify to our office within 30 days of the date of this letter that it has done so.
